fixes.explanation: Paddan-aram is where Jacob lived for years with Laban, and most of his sons were born there (Genesis 35:26). That's Jacob's story, though. Esau's sons were "…born to him in the land of Canaan." (Genesis 36:5) Easy to cross the wires with two brothers and two sets of kids.

Egypt does show up later in Genesis (Genesis 37:28), but not for these five boys. Verse 5 says they "…were born to him in the land of Canaan." (Genesis 36:5) So Canaan is the answer. Egypt is a long walk from Esau's tent, friend, and I wouldn't try it with a cookie box in my mustache.

Not quite, baker. Verse 6 says Esau took "…his livestock, all his other animals, and all the property he had acquired in Canaan…" (Genesis 36:6) So the livestock went right along with him. That's a lot of animals to count at the door.

Esau and Jacob did have trouble over a blessing earlier. Esau speaks to his father Isaac about it in Genesis 27:36. But that's not the reason given here. Verse 7 says, "For their possessions were too great for them to dwell together; the land where they stayed could not support them because of their livestock." (Genesis 36:7) This move comes down to stuff and space.

You got it, baker. Verse 8 says, "So Esau (that is, Edom) settled in the area of Mount Seir." (Genesis 36:8) Verse 9 repeats it and calls him "…the father of the Edomites…" Verse 20 then lists the sons of Seir the Horite, "who were living in the land." (Genesis 36:20)

Mount Carmel is a real mountain in the Bible. Elijah, the prophet, has a showdown with the prophets of Baal there in 1 Kings 18:20-39. But Esau didn't settle there. Verse 8 says, "So Esau (that is, Edom) settled in the area of Mount Seir." (Genesis 36:8) Good mountain, friend, just not his.

Mount Sinai matters a lot later in the Bible, because God speaks the Ten Commandments there (Exodus 20:1-17). But it's not where Esau settled. Verse 8 says, "So Esau (that is, Edom) settled in the area of Mount Seir." (Genesis 36:8) Sinai and Seir both start with S. That's about as far as the match goes.
